documentation.description: DAC1 is the OECD Development Assistance Committee's table of total flows by provider. It reports each donor's ODA, other official flows, export credits and private flows by aid type, with no recipient or sector breakdown. It is the official source for headline ODA, the bilateral and multilateral split, in-donor costs such as refugees in donor countries, and the ODA/GNI ratio.
documentation.attribution: OECD (2026), OECD DAC1, OECD Data Explorer, https://webfs-dcd.oecd.org/files/dotStat/DSD_DAC1/Table1_Data.zip (accessed on 2026-10-12)

transformation_log.description: The OECD publishes DAC1 in April, June, September and December. The complete table is downloaded from the OECD each time it is republished, and replaces the previous copy, so the data reflects the OECD's latest release.

Provider codes are standardised to Data Commons IDs used across the platform, so data can be compared across datasets. The totals DAC1 reports for groups of providers, such as all DAC countries, the G7 and the EU members of the DAC, are kept as providers of their own.

Only figures in current US dollars are included, not constant US dollars or providers' own currencies. Amounts received are left out, though net disbursements, which subtract them, are kept. Where DAC1 reports a grant equivalent under two types of aid, the fuller of the two is used, and total flows as a share of GNI in grant equivalents are left out, since they repeat ODA as a share of GNI.
DAC1 reports amounts, GNI and population in millions, which are converted to whole units.

Every figure is reported against the year and the provider. Flows are broken down by type of aid as DAC1 reports it, and by gross or net disbursements, commitments or grant equivalents, split into grants and non-grants where DAC1 splits them. Shares record that they are a share of the provider's GNI. GNI and population are reported about the provider.

changes.note: Total flows by provider and aid type, including ODA, other official flows and private flows, and ODA as a share of GNI.
